population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma after 1–2 prior lines, ECOG 0–2.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine)
takeaway: Classic ICI pattern — PFS flat or worse, OS clearly better through durable responses. Established pembrolizumab as second-line standard in urothelial carcinoma. Watch the early non-responders who progress fast.

name: KEYNOTE-048
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC; progression within 6 months after chemoradiotherapy was excluded. OC 30%, OP 40%, H 13%, L 25%; TPS ≥50% ~20%, CPS ≥1 ~85%, p16+ 20%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs pembrolizumab + platinum + 5-FU vs EXTREME
endpoints: Pembro mono 16.9% vs 36.0% EXTREME; pembro + chemo 36.3% vs 36.3%
takeaway: Pembrolizumab-based first-line therapy in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC. Monotherapy gives an OS benefit in CPS ≥1 and is less toxic, but PFS and ORR are not improved. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improves OS and ORR in all patients, with a PFS benefit only in CPS ≥20.

name: KEYNOTE-177
population: Treatment-naive dMMR/MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer. 60% right-sided, 40% RAS/BRAF-mutant.
treatment: Pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy (investigator's choice ± bevacizumab/cetuximab)
endpoints: ⚠️ 30% progressed as best response on pembrolizumab
takeaway: Made first-line pembrolizumab standard for dMMR mCRC, with a remarkable 77-month median OS. But 30% have primary resistance and progress immediately — RAS/BRAF-mutant patients may still need chemotherapy, which is the gap CheckMate-8HW's dual blockade addresses.

name: KEYNOTE-181
population: Advanced esophageal cancer, both ESCC and EAC (SCC 64% / adenocarcinoma 36%), after one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy. Asia 39%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 35%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 2 yr vs taxane or irinotecan (open-label)
takeaway: Of three hierarchical co-primary OS endpoints, only CPS ≥10 met its boundary (SCC did not), so the benefit is confined to PD-L1 CPS ≥10 and was FDA approved in CPS ≥10. In contrast, ATTRACTION-3 showed an OS benefit regardless of PD-L1.

name: KEYNOTE-189
population: Treatment-naive metastatic NON-SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level, no EGFR/ALK alteration.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + pemetrexed/platinum vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The trial that established chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard for non-squamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in the numbers.

name: KEYNOTE-224 / KEYNOTE-240
population: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, BCLC B-C.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=278) vs placebo (n=135)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab vs placebo in 2L HCC gave only numerical OS and PFS improvements, as neither crossed its statistical boundary, though ORR was 18.3%. Accelerated approval was nonetheless maintained (ODAC 2021) and later confirmed by KEYNOTE-394.

name: KEYNOTE-355
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, NO CPS requirement for entry. DFI 6–12 mo 20%, >12 mo 50%; de novo metastatic 30%; brain mets 2–6%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + chemo vs placebo + chemo
takeaway: First-line pembrolizumab + chemo improves both PFS and OS — but only at CPS ≥10. Below that, nothing. The sharp contrast with KEYNOTE-522 in early TNBC (where PD-L1 didn't matter at all) is one of the most instructive discrepancies in breast oncology.

name: KEYNOTE-394
population: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; conducted in Asian countries, HBV-positive.
treatment: Pembrolizumab (n=300) vs placebo (n=153)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab beat placebo on OS, PFS and ORR in second-line Asian HCC (progression on or intolerance to sorafenib). It confirms the KEYNOTE-240 signal in an Asian, HBV-predominant population.

name: KEYNOTE-407
population: Treatment-naive metastatic SQUAMOUS NSCLC, any PD-L1 level.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/taxane vs placebo + chemo
endpoints: 📝 Results not captured in your DB — design only
takeaway: The squamous counterpart to KEYNOTE-189, establishing chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard regardless of PD-L1. Worth filling in.

name: KEYNOTE-590
population: Advanced esophageal cancer, both ESCC and EAC (ESCC 73% / adenocarcinoma 27%). Asia 53%; PD-L1 CPS ≥10 in 51%; HER2-positive excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg + cisplatin/5-FU (PF) vs placebo + PF (double-blind, 1:1)
endpoints: ✅ All 45.0% vs 29.3%, P<0.0001; adenoCA 48% vs 25%; mDOR 8.3 vs 6.0 mo
takeaway: Pembrolizumab + PF improved PFS, OS and ORR over PF in first-line ESCC/EAC, making it the standard of care. The benefit is driven by CPS ≥10, with CPS <10 essentially flat (HR 0.86).

name: LEAP-002
population: Advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; Asian 40%; Vp4 excluded.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + lenvatinib vs lenvatinib
takeaway: Pembrolizumab + lenvatinib missed prespecified significance for both OS and PFS versus lenvatinib in first-line unresectable HCC. The lenvatinib control arm was strong (mOS 19.0 mo), and the combination carried more toxicity.

name: MAINTAIN
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (86.5% palbociclib). ≤1 prior chemo line. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy + ribociclib vs switched ET + placebo (NSAI → fulvestrant or exemestane)
takeaway: Switching both the endocrine partner AND the CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib → ribociclib) retains benefit after progression — the first randomised evidence for CDK4/6 inhibitor beyond progression. Benefit was significant in ESR1 wild-type; prior CDK4/6i duration ≤12 months may still leave room.

name: MARIPOSA
population: EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC — Ex19del 60%, L858R 40%. Stable brain mets 40%, with regular brain MRI. Crossover prohibited.
treatment: Amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib vs lazertinib alone — chemotherapy-free
takeaway: A chemotherapy-free amivantamab + lazertinib combination improved both PFS and OS versus osimertinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC, with crossover prohibited. The note attached to this result is to watch for toxicity.

name: MARIPOSA-2
population: EGFR Ex19del or L858R NSCLC progressing on or after osimertinib. Stable brain metastases allowed.
treatment: Amivantamab + chemo (± lazertinib) vs chemotherapy alone
endpoints: ⚠️ 17.7 vs 15.3 mo — numerically higher, not mature
takeaway: Addresses the hardest question in EGFR NSCLC — what to do after osimertinib. Amivantamab + chemo improves PFS, ORR and intracranial PFS. Costs: VTE, haematologic and skin toxicity.

name: MetaGIST
population: Unresectable or metastatic GIST on first-line imatinib. Pooled individual-patient data from two phase III trials (EORTC 62005 and SWOG S0033). Median follow-up 45 months; mutation data in 772 patients.
treatment: Imatinib 800 mg/d vs 400 mg/d, first line
takeaway: Upfront high-dose imatinib buys only a small early PFS advantage and no survival benefit — 400 mg remains the standard starting dose. The single exception is KIT exon 9-mutant GIST, where 800 mg more than doubles response rate.

name: ML18147 (TML)
population: mCRC progressing after first-line bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy. Sidedness not analysed. First line was not anti-EGFR.
treatment: Bevacizumab BEYOND progression + second-line chemo vs chemo alone
takeaway: Continuing bevacizumab past progression with a changed chemotherapy backbone improves survival — regardless of tumour sidedness. Established 'bev beyond progression' as a legitimate strategy.

name: MONALEESA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Ribociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Ribociclib + letrozole delivers both PFS and OS benefit first-line, with median OS exceeding 5 years. Notably, ribociclib has shown OS benefit where palbociclib has not.

name: MONALEESA-3
population: Postmenopausal HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. Half first-line (de novo or relapse >12 mo); half second-line (early relapse ≤12 mo or progression on ET), all CDK4/6i-naive.
treatment: Ribociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Ribociclib works with fulvestrant as well as with an AI, and the OS benefit holds in both first and second line. First-line PFS of 33.6 months is the standout figure.

name: MONALEESA-7
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. One prior line of chemotherapy allowed. The only CDK4/6 trial dedicated to this group.
treatment: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy + ovarian function suppression vs placebo + ET + OFS
takeaway: The only CDK4/6 inhibitor trial designed specifically for premenopausal women, and it delivered both PFS and OS benefit — nearly doubling PFS.

name: MONARCH-2
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy but CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance in ~25%.
treatment: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant improves PFS and OS after endocrine progression, delaying the move to chemotherapy by well over a year.

name: MONARCH-3
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Abemaciclib + non-steroidal AI vs placebo + NSAI
takeaway: Doubles first-line PFS, and the 13-month numerical OS gain narrowly missed significance. Side effects differ from the other CDK4/6 inhibitors: diarrhoea and VTE dominate over neutropenia.

name: MORPHEUS-Liver
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C HCC. Asian 40%.
treatment: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab + tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) (n=40) vs atezolizumab + bevacizumab (n=18)
takeaway: Adding tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) to atezolizumab + bevacizumab improved ORR, PFS and OS in this phase Ib/II first-line unresectable HCC study. The numbers are small (40 vs 18) with an underperforming control arm, and the confirmatory IMbrave152/SKYSCRAPER-14 failed.

name: MOUNTAINEER
population: RAS wild-type, HER2-positive chemorefractory mCRC. Median 2–3 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (vs tucatinib alone)
takeaway: Tucatinib + trastuzumab is active and well tolerated in HER2+ RAS wild-type refractory mCRC — a 24-month median OS in a heavily pretreated population. Led to FDA approval.

name: MVAC (Loehrer)
population: Advanced urothelial carcinoma, cisplatin-eligible.
treatment: MVAC vs single-agent cisplatin
takeaway: The trial that established combination chemotherapy in urothelial carcinoma — more than tripling response rate over single-agent cisplatin. The foundation everything since has been measured against.

name: MyPathway (HER2 CRC cohort)
population: HER2-amplified mCRC, median 4 prior lines. Prior anti-HER2 excluded.
treatment: Trastuzumab + pertuzumab (single-arm basket)
takeaway: Dual HER2 antibody blockade is active and well tolerated in HER2-amplified mCRC, particularly in KRAS wild-type. The short PFS reflects how heavily pretreated these patients were.

name: NALA
population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer after ≥2 prior HER2-directed regimens. ECOG 0–1, 59% HR+, 84% visceral, 16.6% baseline brain mets. Prior: 99.7% trastuzumab, 42% pertuzumab, 54% T-DM1.
treatment: Neratinib + capecitabine vs lapatinib + capecitabine
endpoints: ✅ Fewer CNS interventions 22.8% vs 29.2%, P=0.043; DoR 8.5 vs 5.6 mo
takeaway: The first TKI-versus-TKI superiority trial in metastatic breast cancer. Note the tell-tale pattern — identical median PFS but separated mean PFS, meaning the benefit is in the tail. Grade 3 diarrhoea in 24% despite prophylaxis.

name: NO16966
population: Previously untreated mCRC, ECOG ≤1.
treatment: Bevacizumab + oxaliplatin-based chemo (FOLFOX4 or XELOX) vs chemo alone
takeaway: Bevacizumab improved PFS but not OS or response rate with an oxaliplatin backbone — a weaker effect than with irinotecan. A key subtlety: many patients stopped bevacizumab early for chemo toxicity, which is why the trial argues for continuing bevacizumab until progression.

name: NSABP-B27 (real-world, Jordan)
population: 346 women with high-risk early breast cancer treated neoadjuvantly in Jordan 2003–2014. Median tumour 6.0 cm; 78.3% node-positive — notably more advanced than the original B-27 trial.
treatment: AC ×4 → docetaxel ×4 (single arm)
takeaway: Real-world outcomes matched the trial (pCR 25% vs 26%) despite larger tumours and far more nodal involvement. HR-negative, node-negative and smaller tumours predicted higher pCR. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an early-stage neoadjuvant study — it may belong in the Early DB.

name: OlympiAD
population: Germline BRCA1/2-mutant, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, ≤2 prior metastatic chemo lines. Prior anthracycline and taxane required; prior platinum for metastatic disease EXCLUDED.
treatment: Olaparib vs physician's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First PARP inhibitor trial in breast cancer — PFS benefit, no OS. But an OS signal in the chemotherapy-naive subgroup pointed toward earlier use, which is exactly what OlympiA went on to prove in the adjuvant setting.

name: P025
population: Postmenopausal advanced breast cancer, HR-positive (65%) or unknown (35%). Prior adjuvant endocrine therapy allowed.
treatment: Letrozole vs tamoxifen, first-line for advanced disease
takeaway: Established aromatase inhibitors over tamoxifen as first-line endocrine therapy in advanced disease — the metastatic counterpart to ATAC and BIG 1-98.

name: PALOMA-2
population: Postmenopausal ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, no prior treatment for advanced disease.
treatment: Palbociclib + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole
takeaway: Palbociclib clearly extends PFS but — unlike ribociclib in MONALEESA-2 — never delivered an OS benefit. The central unexplained puzzle of the CDK4/6 class. Main toxicity is myelosuppression.

name: PALOMA-3
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy, CDK4/6i-naive. Any menopausal status; ≤1 prior metastatic chemo line. Primary endocrine resistance ~21%.
treatment: Palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Doubles PFS after endocrine progression. The OS story is subgroup-dependent: no ITT benefit, but a large one in endocrine-sensitive patients — prior endocrine sensitivity predicts who gains.

name: PAOLA-1
population: FIGO III–IV high-grade serous/endometrioid, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer, enrolled regardless of surgical outcome or HRD status. CR 20%, stage III 70%, BRCA mutant 30%, HRD+ ~50%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID × 2 years + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg Q3W × 15 mo vs placebo + bevacizumab
takeaway: Olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance after first-line bevacizumab–taxane–platinum improved PFS and OS in HRD-positive ovarian cancer, and is the only PARP inhibitor trial here with an OS benefit. There was no PFS or OS benefit in HRD-negative patients.

name: PARADIGM
population: RAS wild-type mCRC, ECOG 0–1, prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded. Primary analysis in LEFT-SIDED tumours.
treatment: Panitumumab vs bevacizumab, both with mFOLFOX6
takeaway: The definitive prospective answer to the sidedness question — anti-EGFR first in LEFT-sided RAS wild-type disease, anti-VEGF for right-sided. Depth of response correlated with better OS.

name: PARSIFAL
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, ENDOCRINE-SENSITIVE, no prior treatment for advanced disease. Prior perioperative ET allowed if DFS >12 months.
treatment: Fulvestrant + palbociclib vs letrozole + palbociclib
endpoints: ❌ 27.9 vs 32.8 mo — HR 1.13 (0.89–1.45), P=0.32 — superiority NOT shown
takeaway: Fulvestrant is not a better CDK4/6 partner than an aromatase inhibitor in endocrine-sensitive first-line disease. Keep the NSAI.

name: postMONARCH
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor (60% palbociclib), in either the advanced or early setting. Prior metastatic chemotherapy excluded. Not biomarker-selected.
treatment: SWITCHED endocrine therapy (AI → fulvestrant) + abemaciclib vs switched ET + placebo
takeaway: Confirms in phase III what MAINTAIN suggested — CDK4/6 inhibition beyond progression works, without biomarker selection. Unlike MAINTAIN, prior CDK4/6i duration did not affect the benefit. Be realistic about magnitude: the median PFS gain is under a month.

name: PRIME
population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC, ECOG ≤2. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOX4 vs FOLFOX4
takeaway: Panitumumab + FOLFOX improves both PFS and OS — but only in fully RAS wild-type tumours. The extended RAS analysis of this trial is what expanded testing beyond KRAS exon 2.

name: PYNNACLE
population: Solid tumours carrying the TP53 Y220C mutation (ovary, pancreas, breast, CRC, endometrial, lung, HEENT and others). ECOG 0–1, median 3 prior lines.
treatment: Rezatapopt (PC14586), an oral selective p53 reactivator (single-arm)
endpoints: 20% overall; 30% in KRAS wild-type at ≥1150 mg
takeaway: Proof of concept that a mutant p53 protein can be pharmacologically reactivated — a target considered undruggable for decades. RP2D 2000 mg daily with food; main toxicities GI and anaemia.

name: RAINBOW
population: Metastatic gastric or EGJ adenocarcinoma only (EGJ/esophageal adenocarcinoma 20%) after prior platinum-fluoropyrimidine. Asian 34%, peritoneal metastases 47%.
treatment: Ramucirumab + paclitaxel vs placebo + paclitaxel (no crossover)
takeaway: Ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved PFS, OS and ORR over paclitaxel alone in second-line gastric/EGJ adenocarcinoma, and is the only antiangiogenic to succeed in GC/EGJ. The benefit was larger in EGJ adenocarcinoma than in gastric cancer.

name: RASolute 302
population: Metastatic PDAC, ECOG 0–1, with at least one prior fluoropyrimidine/gemcitabine-based chemotherapy; RAS-mutant (RAS G12X ~100%). Asian ~10%, ECOG 0 50%.
treatment: Daraxonrasib 300 mg PO QD vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: Daraxonrasib improved PFS, OS and ORR over chemotherapy in second-line or later metastatic pancreatic cancer. Median OS of 13.2 months in this setting is a notable result.

name: RATIONALE-301
population: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; VP4 status not specified in the row.
treatment: Tislelizumab vs sorafenib (non-inferiority design)
takeaway: Tislelizumab was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in first-line unresectable HCC, with a higher ORR and far fewer grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events. PFS was worse than with sorafenib.

name: RATIONALE-302
population: ESCC only, after one prior line of chemotherapy; 79% Asian. PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 31%.
treatment: Tislelizumab 200 mg q3w vs investigator's-choice taxane or irinotecan (open-label, 1:1)
endpoints: ❌ 1.6 vs 2.1 mo — HR 0.83 (0.67–1.01); but 12-mo PFS 12.7% vs 1.9% (curves separate after ~3 mo)
takeaway: Tislelizumab improved OS over chemotherapy in second-line ESCC even though median PFS was not better (late curve separation, with a higher 12-month PFS). The benefit concentrates in PD-L1-positive patients (TAP ≥10%), while the TAP <10% subgroup showed only a non-significant trend.

name: RATIONALE-306
population: ESCC only; 75% Asian, 44% had prior definitive treatment. PD-L1 TAP ≥10% in 34%.
treatment: Tislelizumab + chemotherapy (PF or TP) vs placebo + chemotherapy (double-blind, 1:1)
takeaway: Adding tislelizumab to chemotherapy improved PFS, OS and ORR in first-line ESCC. The benefit is driven by patients with TAP ≥10%, while the TAP <10% subgroup had a non-significant OS trend.

name: RATIONALE-309
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic NPC, all Asian (China only). Liver metastases ~40%, baseline EBV-positive ~80%, 75% with prior CCRT.
treatment: Tislelizumab + gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) vs placebo + GP; induction then maintenance; 49% crossover
takeaway: Tislelizumab plus GP improved PFS in first-line recurrent/metastatic NPC, but OS was not significant, with 49% crossover as a confound. The row notes it as the only TFDA-approved option.

name: FOLFOXIRI — GONO
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 62. ECOG 0–1 in 98% — a deliberately FIT population.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (oxaliplatin 85, irinotecan 165, infusional 5-FU 46 h)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy improves response, PFS and OS — but only in genuinely fit patients (98% were ECOG 0–1). Patient selection is the whole story; see the HORG trial for what happens without it.

name: FOLFOXIRI — HORG
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age 66, age ≥75 permitted. ECOG 0 in only 36%, ECOG 2 in 11%. Crossover allowed.
treatment: FOLFOXIRI vs FOLFIRI (lower doses: oxaliplatin 65, irinotecan 150, bolus 5-FU)
takeaway: The negative mirror image of the GONO trial — an older, less fit population, lower drug doses and bolus 5-FU produced no benefit and heavy toxicity. Together the two trials define exactly who FOLFOXIRI is for.

name: REACH-2
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; AFP >400; progression on sorafenib.
treatment: Ramucirumab (n=197) vs placebo (n=95)
takeaway: Ramucirumab improved OS and PFS over placebo in second-line HCC with AFP ≥400. The all-comers REACH-1 was negative, so benefit is restricted to patients with high AFP.

name: RECOURSE
population: Refractory mCRC, median 3 prior regimens, 20% prior regorafenib. ECOG 0 in ~56%.
treatment: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) vs placebo
takeaway: Established TAS-102 as a third-line option in refractory mCRC. Like regorafenib, the benefit is real but small — disease stabilisation rather than response.

name: REFLECT
population: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, BCLC B/C; excluded VP4, bile duct invasion and tumor occupying >50% of the liver.
treatment: Lenvatinib (n=478) vs sorafenib (n=476); non-inferiority design
takeaway: Lenvatinib was non-inferior to sorafenib for OS in first-line unresectable HCC, with better PFS and ORR. The trial excluded VP4, bile duct invasion and ≥50% liver occupation, so those patients are not covered.

name: RESORCE
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤1, progression on sorafenib; only patients who tolerated sorafenib were enrolled.
treatment: Regorafenib (n=379) vs placebo (n=194)
takeaway: Regorafenib improved OS and PFS over placebo in second-line HCC after sorafenib, making it the first second-line approval. It enrolled only patients who tolerated sorafenib, so the result does not apply to sorafenib-intolerant patients.

name: ReTrITA
population: Refractory mCRC after ≥2 prior lines.
treatment: Sequencing study — regorafenib → TAS-102 vs TAS-102 → regorafenib
endpoints: ✅ 11.5 vs 8.5 mo — HR 0.60 (0.49–0.74), P<0.0001 (monotherapy PFS nearly identical: 3.2 vs 3.3 mo)
takeaway: Sequence matters — regorafenib first, then TAS-102. Note the tell: each drug's individual PFS is identical, so the benefit comes from the ordering, not from either agent. Retrospective, so treat with appropriate caution.

name: RIGHT Choice
population: PRE/PERI-MENOPAUSAL women with aggressive HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer — including visceral crisis — with no prior treatment for advanced disease. The population clinicians reflexively give chemotherapy.
treatment: Ribociclib + NSAI + ovarian function suppression vs investigator's-choice combination chemotherapy
takeaway: Directly challenges the instinct to reach for chemotherapy in visceral crisis — endocrine therapy plus ribociclib gave 9 months more PFS with better tolerability. Practice-changing for aggressive premenopausal HR+ disease.

name: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib, CRC)
population: RAS-mutant refractory colorectal cancer (details not yet captured).
treatment: RMC-6236 (daraxonrasib) — RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for the colorectal cohort of daraxonrasib. Worth filling in — the same drug produced a doubling of OS in pancreatic cancer (RASolute 302).

name: Saltz et al.
population: Previously untreated mCRC, median age ~60. Over half were ECOG 1–2; 80% had liver metastases.
treatment: Irinotecan + 5-FU/LV (IFL) vs 5-FU/LV vs irinotecan alone
takeaway: The trial that moved metastatic colorectal cancer from single-agent fluorouracil to doublet chemotherapy, lifting response rates from ~20% to 50%. The starting point of the modern mCRC treatment sequence.

name: SERENA-6
population: ER+/HER2− advanced breast cancer with an EMERGENT ESR1 mutation detected on ctDNA surveillance during first-line AI + CDK4/6i (≥6 months), with NO radiographic progression yet. A genuinely novel entry criterion.
treatment: Switch to camizestrant + continue the same CDK4/6 inhibitor vs continue AI + CDK4/6i
takeaway: The first trial to act on a molecular relapse before it becomes a radiographic one — switching endocrine partner on emergent ESR1 ctDNA nearly doubles PFS while keeping the CDK4/6 inhibitor. A new treatment paradigm, though OS is not yet known.

name: SHARP
population: Child-Pugh A, ECOG ≤2; more than 80% from Europe and Australasia.
treatment: Sorafenib (n=299) vs placebo (n=303)
takeaway: Sorafenib improved OS and PFS over placebo in first-line advanced HCC and became the first systemic standard of care. Objective response was about 0%, so the benefit comes from stable disease (DCR 43% vs 32%).

name: SOFT (adjuvant)
population: Pre/perimenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer — adjuvant setting.
treatment: Tamoxifen alone vs tamoxifen + OFS vs exemestane + OFS
takeaway: High-risk premenopausal women benefit from ovarian function suppression. Note: this row sits in your Metastatic DB but is an adjuvant trial, and largely duplicates the SOFT/TEXT entry in your Early DB — worth consolidating.

name: SOHO-01
population: HER2-mutant NSCLC (details not yet captured).
treatment: Sevabertinib (BAY 2927088) — HER2-selective TKI
endpoints: 📝 Row is a placeholder — results not captured yet
takeaway: Placeholder for sevabertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC — a sibling to zongertinib (Beamion Lung-01). Worth filling both in together for comparison.

name: SOLAR-1
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer in men and postmenopausal women, relapsed or progressed on an AI; no chemotherapy in the advanced setting; prior CDK4/6i 6%. Primary analysis in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort; patients with diabetes or poor glycemic control excluded.
treatment: Alpelisib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
takeaway: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant improved PFS but not OS in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after an AI. Bone-only disease appears to derive no benefit, and severe hyperglycemia is a notable toxicity.

name: Sorafenib in desmoid tumour
population: Progressive, symptomatic or recurrent desmoid tumours. Median age 37, 69% female, 40% prior systemic therapy, 50% prior surgery. Crossover allowed at progression.
treatment: Sorafenib 400 mg daily vs placebo
endpoints: ✅ 33% vs 20% — median time to response 9.6 mo
takeaway: First randomised phase III in desmoid tumours, with a striking 87% reduction in progression risk. Two clinical lessons: responses are late (median 9.6 months) so don't abandon stable disease early, and the 20% placebo response rate supports watchful waiting as a first move. 20% discontinued for skin toxicity.

name: STELLAR-303
population: MSS/pMMR refractory mCRC — a true third line: all had received 5-FU, irinotecan and oxaliplatin; no prior regorafenib, TAS-102 or ICI; BRAF-mutant required prior BRAF-targeted therapy.
treatment: Zanzalintinib + atezolizumab vs regorafenib
takeaway: Immunotherapy finally shows an OS signal in MSS colorectal cancer — but with a modest 1.5-month gain and substantially more toxicity. Weigh carefully in a late-line population.

name: SUNLIGHT
population: Refractory mCRC — >90% had exactly 2 prior lines. ECOG 0 in 43–48%.
treatment: TAS-102 + bevacizumab vs TAS-102 alone
endpoints: ✅ No prior bev HR 0.40 vs prior bev HR 0.72
takeaway: Adding bevacizumab to TAS-102 more than doubles PFS and gives a 3.3-month OS gain — the best third-line result in mCRC. Benefit is much larger in bevacizumab-naive patients.

name: TRIBE
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~90%; right-sided 25–35%.
treatment: Bevacizumab + FOLFOXIRI (triplet) vs bevacizumab + FOLFIRI (doublet)
takeaway: Triplet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab improves OS in fit patients. Subgroup analysis supports it particularly for right-sided tumours, where anti-EGFR does not work.

name: TRIBE2
population: All-comer mCRC, unselected for RAS/BRAF or sidedness. ECOG 0 in ~85%; right-sided 40%.
treatment: Upfront bevacizumab-triplet (with reintroduction after progression) vs sequential bevacizumab-doublet
takeaway: Confirms TRIBE with a strategy endpoint — giving the triplet upfront, then reintroducing it, beats sequential doublets on PFS2 and OS. Particularly relevant for right-sided disease.

name: TriComB
population: UNFIT, elderly mCRC — median age 80, ECOG 1 in ~55%, RAS-mutant ~80%.
treatment: TAS-102 + capecitabine + bevacizumab
takeaway: A chemo-light triplet for patients too frail for standard doublets — 55% response and 10 months PFS at a median age of 80 is a strong early signal. Randomised confirmation pending.

name: TRIPLETE
population: RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC, left-sided 88%, ECOG 0 in ~80%. Prior adjuvant oxaliplatin excluded.
treatment: Panitumumab + FOLFOXIRI vs panitumumab + FOLFOX
endpoints: ✅ 41.1 vs 33.3 mo — HR 0.79 (0.63–0.99), P=0.049 — inconsistent with the primary result
takeaway: In RAS/BRAF wild-type disease, anti-EGFR plus a doublet is already good enough — the triplet adds toxicity without improving response or PFS. Treat the borderline OS finding with scepticism given the negative primary endpoint.

name: TROPION-Breast02
population: Treatment-naive metastatic TNBC, ICI-INELIGIBLE. No DFI requirement — deliberately includes the worst-prognosis first-line patients: DFI 0–6 mo 15%, de novo 34%, brain mets 10%.
treatment: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
takeaway: First-line Dato-DXd improves BOTH PFS and OS in ICI-ineligible metastatic TNBC — and did so in a deliberately poor-prognosis population (the highest brain-met and short-DFI proportions of any first-line TNBC trial). Sits alongside ASCENT-03 as the answer for CPS <10 disease.

name: VIKTORIA-1
population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, PIK3CA wild-type, progressing on CDK4/6i + NSAI.
treatment: Gedatolisib + fulvestrant ± palbociclib vs fulvestrant (open-label)
endpoints: ✅ 9.3 (triplet) vs 7.4 (doublet) vs 2.0 (fulvestrant) — triplet HR 0.24 (0.17–0.35), p<0.001; doublet HR 0.33 (0.24–0.48), p<0.001
takeaway: In PIK3CA wild-type HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6i + NSAI, gedatolisib plus fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, improved PFS. The OS hazard ratios were not significant, and the triplet regimen caused neutropenia.

name: ATTRACTION-5
population: Pathological stage IIIA–C gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after gastrectomy with D2+ lymph-node dissection. Asian only (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China).
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab added to chemotherapy did not improve RFS after D2 gastrectomy for stage III gastric/GEJ cancer. It is the first phase 3 of adjuvant ICI after D2 surgery in Asia and it is negative, in contrast with the perioperative approaches tested in KEYNOTE-585 and MATTERHORN. The nivolumab arm paid for it in toxicity — endocrine adverse events 21% vs 3% and more discontinuations — with no efficacy in return.

name: CheckMate-141
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC progressing within 6 months of platinum given either as adjuvant therapy or as first-line treatment for metastatic disease. Oral cavity 50%, oropharynx 35%, larynx 14%. Prior cetuximab 62%, ≥2 prior lines 55%, PD-L1 ≥1% 57%.
treatment: Nivolumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel or cetuximab), randomised 2:1
takeaway: Nivolumab monotherapy improves overall survival in platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic HNSCC without improving PFS — the gain is in the tail of the curve, not the early one. Benefit is concentrated in PD-L1-positive disease and vanishes below 1%. Its entry criteria were broader than KEYNOTE-040's: patients recurring within 3 months of definitive platinum-based therapy were eligible here.

name: CheckMate-238
population: R0 resected stage IIIB, IIIC or IV cutaneous melanoma (AJCC7; no IIIA). Resected brain mets allowed (24% with brain mets in M disease). IIIB 35%, IIIC 45%, IV ~20%; BRAF-mutant 40%.
treatment: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w vs ipilimumab 10 mg/kg IV q3w ×4 → q12w (both ≤1 year)
endpoints: ↔️ 9-yr 69% vs 65%, median NR (>9 yr) in both — HR 0.88 (95.03% CI 0.69–1.11); melanoma-specific HR 0.87 (0.67–1.13)
takeaway: One year of adjuvant nivolumab improved RFS and DMFS over ipilimumab and is the standard of care, with far less toxicity than ipilimumab. OS did not differ, which is attributed to the active comparator.

name: CheckMate-511
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 wk earlier. Active brain mets excluded.
treatment: NIVO3 + IPI1 ×4 vs NIVO1 + IPI3 ×4, then nivolumab 480 mg q4w maintenance
endpoints: ↔️ NR vs NR; 12-mo 79.7% vs 81.0% — HR 1.09 (0.73–1.62), descriptive
takeaway: Flipping from NIVO1 + IPI3 (as in CM-067) to NIVO3 + IPI1 gave a better safety profile, the primary endpoint, with similar efficacy. The efficacy endpoints are descriptive only, and there is no comparison to nivolumab monotherapy.

name: CheckMate-76K
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery; ocular and mucosal melanoma excluded. IIB 60%; superficial spreading 30%, nodular 50%, acral 5%; BRAF V600E-mutant 28–30%.
treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg q4w × 1 yr vs placebo, randomised 2:1
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas COUNTED as RFS events and death COUNTED as a DMFS event — unlike KEYNOTE-716
takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year more than halves the recurrence hazard in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, with a matching distant-metastasis benefit. There is still no OS report, and the price is real: 50% discontinued for adverse events and 15% needed hormone replacement for endocrine immune toxicity. Because it counts new primary melanomas as RFS events where KEYNOTE-716 does not, the two trials' hazard ratios are not directly comparable.

name: CheckMate-915
population: Completely resected stage IIIB–D or IV melanoma (AJCC 8th); complete lymph-node dissection NOT required. Cutaneous ~88%, acral ~3%, mucosal ~1%; stage IV 13%; BRAF-mutant 31%.
treatment: Nivolumab 240 mg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w vs nivolumab 480 mg q4w + placebo — both ≤1 year
endpoints: ⚠️ 2-yr 89.8% vs 91.8% — HR 1.09 (0.80–1.32), immature and numerically favours nivolumab alone
takeaway: Adding low-dose ipilimumab to adjuvant nivolumab failed both co-primary RFS endpoints and DMFS, with immature OS running numerically the wrong way — single-agent nivolumab, as in CheckMate-238, is enough. The one useful design lesson is that enrolling patients who had not had a completion lymph-node dissection did not degrade RFS.

name: COMBI-AD
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th) carrying a BRAF V600E (90%) or V600K mutation. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%.
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ 3-yr 86% vs 77% — HR 0.57 (0.42–0.79), P=0.0006 against a required P=0.000019, so not significant
takeaway: One year of adjuvant dabrafenib/trametinib halves the recurrence hazard and improves DMFS in resected BRAF V600-mutant stage III melanoma; OS improved numerically but never crossed the extremely stringent interim boundary. It makes targeted therapy a legitimate adjuvant option in BRAF-mutant disease — but DREAMseq later showed that in the metastatic setting ICI should come before BRAF/MEK inhibition.

name: DREAMseq
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III or IV melanoma with a BRAF V600E/K mutation (V600E 82%, V600K 12%). Excluded any prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4 or BRAF/MEK, even in the neo/adjuvant setting (prior adjuvant 12–16%); treated brain mets allowed.
treatment: Sequence A/C: nivolumab + ipilimumab first, then dabrafenib/trametinib after progression. Sequence B/D: dabrafenib/trametinib first, then nivolumab + ipilimumab after progression. Nivo/ipi was followed by maintenance nivolumab.
takeaway: In BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma, nivolumab/ipilimumab should precede BRAF/MEK inhibition, with benefit in OS, duration of response and second-line ORR. The advantage comes from the second line: TKIs still work after dual ICI, but dual ICI works poorly in the second line. Crossover occurred in only about 50%, so first-line treatment matters most.

name: EORTC 18071
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th); LDH >2× ULN excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 40%. BRAF status not prespecified.
treatment: Ipilimumab 10 mg/kg q3w ×4 then q12w for up to 3 years vs placebo
takeaway: The first adjuvant melanoma trial to show an overall survival benefit, proving that adjuvant checkpoint blockade can do more than delay recurrence. It is a landmark rather than a current option: high-dose ipilimumab was so toxic that the median patient received only 4 doses of a planned 3-year course, and it was superseded by adjuvant nivolumab in CheckMate-238.

name: EXTREME
population: Treatment-naive recurrent/metastatic HNSCC with detectable EGFR expression.
treatment: Platinum + 5-FU + cetuximab (400 → 250 mg/m² weekly) vs platinum + 5-FU alone; chemotherapy q3w for up to 6 cycles
takeaway: Adding cetuximab to platinum/5-FU improved response, PFS and overall survival, making it the first-line standard of care in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC until KEYNOTE-048 displaced it. The cost is more sepsis and hypomagnesaemia.

name: INFINITY
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H, EBV-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (Italian GONO). Cohort 1 (n=18) cT≥2 any N M0 proceeds to surgery; cohort 2 (n=18) cT2–3 any N M0 goes to definitive non-operative management if a clinical CR is achieved (T4 excluded after cohort 1).
treatment: Chemo-free tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w ×3 (T300/D), single arm
endpoints: ⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Chemo-free neoadjuvant tremelimumab + durvalumab produced a 60% pCR and 80% major pathological response in resectable MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, reproducing NEONIPIGA. Cohort 2 provides the first prospective feasibility data for organ preservation in this disease — 76% reached a clinical CR and avoided surgery, with a single local regrowth salvaged surgically. T4 tumours respond far less well (pCR 17% vs 89%), linked to an M2-macrophage-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment, and are now excluded from the non-operative cohort.

name: INT-0099
population: Stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma (AJCC/UICC), no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, performance status 0–2.
treatment: Concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation → adjuvant cisplatin/5-FU vs radiotherapy alone
endpoints: ✅ NR vs 15 mo; 3-yr 66% vs 26% — HR 4.34 (2.47–7.69) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P<0.001
✅ NR vs 34 mo; 3-yr 76% vs 46% — HR 2.50 (1.29–4.84) for RT alone vs chemoradiation, P=0.005
takeaway: The landmark trial that made concurrent cisplatin chemoradiation followed by adjuvant chemotherapy the standard of care in stage III–IV nasopharyngeal carcinoma, roughly doubling 3-year PFS and OS over radiotherapy alone. Read the hazard ratios carefully: they are expressed with radiotherapy alone in the numerator, so values above 1 favour chemoradiation.

name: KEYNOTE-585
population: Untreated, locally advanced, resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (T3 or deeper, or node-positive, M0). Global — 143 centres in 24 countries, 47% Asia.
treatment: Neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab + chemotherapy vs placebo + chemotherapy on a cisplatin/capecitabine or 5-FU backbone (separate FLOT safety cohort, n=203)
endpoints: ⚠️ 44.4 vs 25.3 mo — HR 0.81 (0.67–0.99), P=0.0198 against a boundary of P<0.0178, so not met; 2-yr EFS 58% vs 51%
takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab produced a large pCR gain but missed the prespecified EFS significance boundary by a hair (P=0.0198 vs the required 0.0178), and OS was not significant. It is the first global phase 3 of perioperative ICI in resectable gastric/GEJ cancer and a near-miss, contrasting with the subsequently positive MATTERHORN. The main cohort did not use FLOT as the chemotherapy backbone, which limits how far the result travels outside Asia.

name: KEYNOTE-040
population: Recurrent/metastatic HNSCC with progression on platinum, or recurrence within 3–6 months of platinum-based definitive therapy — a narrower population than CheckMate-141. Prior cetuximab 60%, ≥2 prior lines ~30%, PD-L1 ≥1% 80%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy vs investigator's choice (methotrexate, docetaxel, cetuximab); crossover 13%
takeaway: Pembrolizumab monotherapy improved overall survival but not PFS in platinum-refractory, PD-L1-positive HNSCC. The eligible population was narrower than CheckMate-141's, admitting only recurrence within 3–6 months of definitive platinum-based therapy.

name: KEYNOTE-054
population: Completely resected stage IIIA (nodal deposit >1 mm), IIIB or IIIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 7th). IIIA 15%, IIIB 45%, IIIC 37%; BRAF V600-mutant 40–45%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 18 doses (~1 yr) vs placebo
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab became a standard of care in resected stage III melanoma, cutting the recurrence hazard by roughly 43% with a matching distant-metastasis benefit, and it works regardless of PD-L1 status. OS is still immature, and — unlike CheckMate-238 — no stage IV patients were enrolled, so the result does not extend to resected metastatic disease.

name: KEYNOTE-716
population: Resected stage IIB or IIC cutaneous melanoma (AJCC 8th), no treatment other than surgery. IIB 65%. Histological subtype and BRAF status were deliberately not prespecified for subgroup analysis.
treatment: Adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w × 1 yr vs placebo
endpoints: ⚠️ New primary melanomas NOT counted as RFS events and death NOT counted as a DMFS event — unlike CheckMate-76K
takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab improves RFS and DMFS in resected stage IIB–IIC melanoma, the stage-II counterpart to CheckMate-76K. Check the endpoint definitions before comparing the two: this trial excluded new primary melanomas from RFS events and deaths from DMFS events, where CheckMate-76K counted both. OS is immature, and BRAF and PD-L1 subgroups were deliberately not prespecified.

name: NADINA
population: Stage IIIB–IIID melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease. Unknown primary 20%, in-transit metastases 10%; T2 20%, T3 20%, T4 25%; BRAF-mutant 50%.
treatment: Perioperative nivolumab 240 mg + ipilimumab 80 mg q3w ×2 → therapeutic lymph node dissection → response-driven therapy (nothing further after a major pathological response; dabrafenib/trametinib ×46 wk if BRAF-mutant, nivolumab ×11 if wild-type) vs adjuvant control (TLND → nivolumab 480 mg q4w ×12)
endpoints: ✅ pCR 47.2% + near-pCR 11.8% = MPR 59.0%; by BRAF, mutant 53.8% vs wild-type 65.3%; radiologic ORR at wk 6 35.8%
⏳ Blinded until the prespecified final analysis, 3 years after the last patient is enrolled
takeaway: Two cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab/ipilimumab before lymph node dissection cut the event hazard by two-thirds versus standard adjuvant nivolumab, and 59% of patients achieved a major pathological response and needed no further therapy at all. It also establishes pathological response as predictive of survival — 12-month RFS runs from 95% in major responders down to 57% in non-responders — which is what makes response-driven escalation and de-escalation possible. OS is still blinded.

name: NEONIPIGA
population: Resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2–T4 N0/1 M0, ECOG 0–1, age ≤75; French GERCOR study across 11 centres.
treatment: Neoadjuvant nivolumab + low-dose ipilimumab → surgery → adjuvant nivolumab (single arm)
endpoints: Not reached at 14.9-mo median follow-up; 30/31 (97%) eligible patients alive and event-free (1 postoperative death)
Not reached; 30/31 (97%) alive at data cutoff
⚠️ Single-arm — no DFS, no hazard ratios
takeaway: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab produced a 58.6% pCR in resectable dMMR/MSI-H gastric/GEJ cancer, far above the ~3–11% historically achieved with chemotherapy, with 100% R0 resection and manageable immune-related toxicity. It raised the question of a watch-and-wait, non-operative strategy for MSI-H gastric cancer, tested prospectively in INFINITY cohort 2. Neither PD-L1 CPS nor Lynch-versus-sporadic status predicted pathological response.

name: PRODIGY
population: Korean, ECOG 0–1, cT2–3 node-positive or cT4 any N gastric cancer (AJCC 7th). Stage III 80%.
treatment: Neoadjuvant DOS (docetaxel/oxaliplatin/S-1) ×3 → surgery → adjuvant S-1 vs surgery → adjuvant S-1
endpoints: 10.4% (23/222) in the neoadjuvant arm; not applicable to the surgery-first arm
⚠️ 3-yr 74.2% vs 73.4% — HR 0.84 (0.60–1.19), P=0.338; immature and underpowered
takeaway: The first Asian phase 3 to show that adding neoadjuvant chemotherapy to surgery plus adjuvant S-1 improves progression-free survival in locally advanced gastric cancer. The gain did not carry through to overall survival — the OS analysis was immature and underpowered — so it supports rather than proves the perioperative approach in a D2-gastrectomy population.

name: RELATIVITY-047
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III or IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 months earlier. Active CNS metastases excluded; BRAF-mutant 38%.
treatment: Relatlimab 160 mg + nivolumab 480 mg vs nivolumab alone (Q4W)
takeaway: Relatlimab plus nivolumab improved PFS, ORR and OS over nivolumab alone in first-line melanoma, making it the first positive LAG-3 trial. PD-L1 is not predictive of efficacy.

name: SWOG S1801
population: Resectable stage IIIB–IIID or oligometastatic stage IV melanoma (AJCC 8th) with clinically overt nodal disease (resectable node >1.5 cm short axis). Prior ICI and brain metastases excluded. IIIB 40%, IIIC 45%; acral 3%, mucosal 3%; BRAF-mutant ~25%.
treatment: Perioperative pembrolizumab ×3 → surgery → pembrolizumab ×15 vs surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab ×18 — 200 mg q3w, 18 total doses in both arms
endpoints: ⏳ Immature — 36 deaths in total (14 vs 22), too few for a definitive comparison
takeaway: Giving the same total amount of pembrolizumab but moving three doses in front of surgery improved 2-year event-free survival by over 20 percentage points. It is the proof of concept that neoadjuvant ICI beats purely adjuvant ICI — sequence, not dose or duration, is what changed. OS is still immature.

name: CheckMate-067
population: Treatment-naive unresectable stage III–IV melanoma; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 wk earlier. Active brain mets excluded. BRAF-mutant 31.5%.
treatment: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w vs nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + placebo vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w ×4 + placebo
endpoints: ✅ 11.5 vs 6.9 vs 2.9 mo; 3-yr PFS 39% vs 32% vs 10% — HR vs ipilimumab 0.42 (0.31–0.57) for nivo+ipi and 0.57 (0.43–0.76) for nivo, both P<0.001
✅ NR vs 37.6 vs 19.9 mo; 3-yr OS 58% vs 52% vs 34% — HR vs ipilimumab 0.55 (0.45–0.69) for nivo+ipi and 0.65 (0.53–0.80) for nivo, both P<0.001
takeaway: Nivolumab with or without ipilimumab beat ipilimumab alone on PFS, OS and ORR in melanoma. The combination was significantly more toxic.

name: ARASENS
population: mHSPC with no prior treatment allowed. Visceral metastases in 17%.
treatment: Darolutamide 600 mg BID + ADT + docetaxel (triplet) vs placebo + ADT + docetaxel
takeaway: Adding darolutamide to ADT plus docetaxel improved OS and the other secondary endpoints, so triplet therapy is the first-line choice for patients fit for docetaxel. Cardiac disorders are the side effect to watch.

name: ARCHES
population: mHSPC, high-volume disease 63%, Gleason ≥8 67%. Prior treatment allowed: prior docetaxel 18%; prior ADT ≤3 mo 72%, >3 mo 20%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Enzalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS, OS and the other key secondary endpoints, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Side effects to watch are hypertension and CNS effects (fatigue, cognitive decline).

name: CHAARTED
population: Treatment-naive mHSPC (prior adjuvant ADT allowed if completed ≥12 mo earlier). Prespecified high-volume disease (visceral mets or ≥4 bone mets with ≥1 non-axial) in ~65%; ~60% Gleason ≥8; 75% de novo.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel (75 mg/m² q3w × 6) vs ADT alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT improved OS and time to CRPC in mHSPC, with the OS benefit seen in high-volume disease. No benefit was observed in low-volume disease.

name: ENZAMET
population: mHSPC; high-volume 52%, Gleason ≥8 60%. Prior treatment allowed: 45% planned early docetaxel, 50% anti-androgen, 70% ADT.
treatment: Enzalutamide + ADT (± early docetaxel) vs standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide/nilutamide/flutamide) + ADT (± early docetaxel)
takeaway: Enzalutamide + ADT improved clinical PFS and OS, along with the other key secondary endpoints, versus first-generation anti-androgens + ADT. The OS benefit was attenuated in the planned-docetaxel subgroup.

name: CAPItello-281
population: PTEN-deficient de novo mHSPC; 60% high-risk and 74% high-volume disease, Gleason ≥8 in about 80%. Prior abiraterone allowed (~10%); no prior chemotherapy.
treatment: Capivasertib + abiraterone + ADT vs placebo + abiraterone + ADT (capivasertib 400 mg BID, 4 days on / 3 days off)
takeaway: Adding capivasertib to abiraterone + ADT improved rPFS and the other secondary endpoints in PTEN-loss mCSPC. OS is immature, and side effects included hyperglycemia, diarrhea and rash.

name: GETUG-AFU 15
population: Metastatic, hormone-sensitive (non-castrate) prostate cancer, N=385 (192 vs 193). Metastatic at initial diagnosis 67% (docetaxel arm) / 75% (ADT-alone arm); median age 63–64; 81% bone mets.
treatment: ADT + docetaxel vs ADT alone
takeaway: Adding docetaxel to ADT did not improve OS in this trial (HR 1.01), in contrast to CHAARTED, even though it improved all secondary endpoints (biochemical PFS, clinical PFS, PSA response). OS was confounded by crossover: 62% of the ADT-alone arm received docetaxel at castration resistance versus only 28% re-treated in the docetaxel arm. Median OS was longer than in historical series in both arms (54–59 months), suggesting the trial may have been underpowered for the effect size assumed in its sample-size calculation.

name: LATITUDE
population: Treatment-naive, high-risk metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (≥2 of 3: Gleason ≥8, ≥3 bone mets, visceral mets); prior treatment not allowed. 96% had Gleason ≥8 + ≥3 bone mets.
treatment: Abiraterone + prednisone + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Adding abiraterone + prednisone to ADT improved rPFS, OS and the other key secondary endpoints in high-risk, treatment-naive mHSPC. Side effects reflect mineralocorticoid excess (hypertension, hypokalemia).

name: PEACE-1
population: De novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; 60.6% received docetaxel, 43.1% low-volume (CHAARTED criteria).
treatment: 2×2 factorial: standard of care (ADT ± docetaxel) ± abiraterone, ± prostate RT (74 Gy/37 fr)
endpoints: rPFS (1°), low-volume, RT + abiraterone vs abiraterone alone
rPFS (1°), low-volume, RT vs no RT (no abiraterone)
rPFS (1°), ITT, abiraterone + RT vs abiraterone alone
OS (1°), ITT, pooled RT vs no RT
❌ No OS benefit from adding RT — HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.83–1.14), P=0.75
takeaway: Adding prostate RT improved rPFS only in one scenario: RT plus abiraterone in low-volume disease. Adding RT also delayed progression to CRPC, but it gave no OS benefit overall.

name: INT-0162 (SWOG S9346)
population: Treatment-naive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, ECOG 0–2. Gleason ≥8 ~20%, visceral mets 6–7%, extensive disease ~50%.
treatment: Non-inferiority design: 7-mo ADT + bicalutamide, randomized if PSA ≤4 to continuous ADT vs intermittent ADT (intermittent: resume ADT when PSA ≥20 or back to baseline for 7 mo, then stop once PSA ≤4)
takeaway: Intermittent ADT appeared non-inferior to continuous ADT, but the non-inferiority boundary was not statistically met, so it cannot be said that intermittent ADT was significantly inferior or non-inferior. Continuous ADT remained the standard of care.

name: HERO
setting: N/A — mixed disease settings, not metastatic-specific
population: ⚠️ Mixed population: 31.7% metastatic (22.7% de novo), 50.2% relapsed non-metastatic, 27.1% locally advanced. A head-to-head ADT-formulation trial; the trial did not assess oncologic efficacy (PFS/OS NA).
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide
endpoints: ✅ 96.7% vs 88.8% (testosterone <50 ng/dL through 48 wk) — +7.9%, P<0.001 for superiority
takeaway: Oral relugolix achieved superior sustained castration and a 54% lower rate of major adverse cardiovascular events than the GnRH agonist leuprolide. The population is mixed across disease settings and the trial did not assess oncologic efficacy.

name: HERO
population: ⚠️ Cross-listed from the Metastatic database: the population spans multiple disease settings — 50.2% biochemical/clinical relapse after curative local therapy, 27.1% advanced localized disease unsuitable for curative local intervention, 31.7% metastatic (22.7% newly diagnosed androgen-sensitive). It is an ADT-formulation comparison with pharmacodynamic/cardiovascular endpoints rather than DFS/OS/pCR.
treatment: Relugolix (oral GnRH antagonist) vs leuprolide (injectable LHRH agonist), both as androgen-deprivation therapy
endpoints: 96.7% vs 88.8% (testosterone <50 ng/dL through 48 wk) — diff 7.9 pts (95% CI 4.1–11.8), P<0.001 for superiority
takeaway: Oral relugolix achieved rapid, sustained testosterone suppression statistically superior to injectable leuprolide, with no testosterone surge (castrate by day 4 vs a surge to ~625 ng/dL with leuprolide). It was associated with a 54% lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, most pronounced in patients with pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors (>90% of the trial population). This is the same trial as the Metastatic database entry, cross-listed here because the population is mostly non-metastatic; it is not a curative-intent treatment-intensification trial.

name: STAMPEDE (Docetaxel, Arm C)
population: Treatment-naive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, ~95% de novo, ~70% Gleason ≥8. CHAARTED burden assessable in 76%: 44% low-burden, 56% high-burden.
treatment: SOC (ADT) + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV Q3W ×6 + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs SOC (ADT) alone (2:1)
endpoints: ✅ Low-burden 93.2 vs 76.7; ✅ high-burden 39.9 vs 35.2 — ↔ no heterogeneity (interaction P=0.827)
takeaway: Docetaxel added to ADT improved OS in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer regardless of metastatic burden (compared with CHAARTED), and also improved FFS, PFS, mPFS and PCSS. STAMPEDE's low-burden subgroup was larger (n=362).

name: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M1
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer from STAMPEDE Arm G (trial-wide 75% M1, 25% M0); Gleason ≥8 in 75%.
treatment: ADT + abiraterone 1000 mg QD + prednisolone 5 mg QD vs ADT alone
endpoints: ✅ Trial-wide RMST over 54 mo 43.9 vs 30.0 (Δ13.9) — HR 0.31 (0.26–0.37)
↔ No heterogeneity of effect (interaction P=0.37 OS, P=0.08 FFS)
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT improved both FFS and OS in this hormone-sensitive population. The benefit did not differ by metastatic status, and several figures are trial-wide (M1 plus M0) rather than M1-only.

name: STAMPEDE (Abiraterone, Arm G) — M0
population: Non-metastatic (M0) pre-specified subgroup of STAMPEDE's abiraterone comparison (n=915 of 1917 total): node-positive, or node-negative high-risk locally advanced (≥2 of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL) disease starting long-term ADT, or relapsing after prior radical local therapy with high-risk features. RT was mandatory (node-negative) or encouraged (node-positive); reported RT use ~39–40% in both arms.
treatment: SOC (ADT) + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg once daily vs SOC (ADT) alone
endpoints: ⏳ Deaths 34/460 (7%) vs 44/455 (10%) — HR 0.75 (0.48–1.18), immature (78 deaths trial-wide in M0)
↔ No heterogeneity vs M1 subgroup (interaction P=0.37 OS, P=0.08 FFS)
takeaway: Adding abiraterone to ADT plus RT markedly improved failure-free survival in the non-metastatic subgroup (HR 0.21), even though abiraterone was capped at 2 years here. The OS signal (HR 0.75) is directionally favourable but immature with only 78 deaths, and there was no heterogeneity versus the metastatic subgroup; grade 3–5 AEs were more frequent than with ADT alone (47% vs 33% trial-wide), mainly hypertension and hepatic.

name: TITAN
population: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; high-volume disease 63%, Gleason ≥8 67%. Prior treatment allowed, including prior docetaxel (11%).
treatment: Apalutamide 240 mg/day + ADT vs placebo + ADT
takeaway: Apalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS and (at interim analysis) OS, and the other key secondary endpoints were also positive, with benefit regardless of disease burden and prior treatment. Reported side effects were rash, hypothyroidism and ischaemic heart disease.

name: ARTEMIS-008
population: SCLC after first-line chemotherapy. Stable brain metastases 20%, prior ICI 80%, chemo-free interval <90 d ~36%.
treatment: Risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) 8 mg/kg Q3W vs topotecan 1.2 mg/m² D1–5 Q3W
takeaway: Ris-Rez improved PFS and OS over topotecan in second-line SCLC, and is the first B7-H3 ADC with an OS benefit. Watch for ILD and hematologic toxicity.

name: AFFIRM
population: mCRPC after docetaxel. ECOG 2 in 9%; visceral (liver/lung) metastases in 23%.
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS over placebo in mCRPC after docetaxel. Side effects to watch include fatigue and seizure.

name: COU-AA-301
population: mCRPC after docetaxel; ECOG 2 in 10%, bone mets ~89%, liver mets 10%, median PSA ~130.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisolone improved rPFS and OS over placebo + prednisolone in mCRPC after docetaxel. Side effects are mineralocorticoid-related.

name: COU-AA-302
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC with no visceral metastases.
treatment: Abiraterone 1000 mg/d + prednisolone 5 mg BID vs placebo + prednisolone
takeaway: Abiraterone + prednisolone improved rPFS and OS over placebo in pre-docetaxel mCRPC. Visceral metastases were excluded, and the OS HR crossed the efficacy boundary only at the fourth interim analysis.

name: PREVAIL
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC. Visceral metastases allowed (~12%).
treatment: Enzalutamide 160 mg/d vs placebo
takeaway: Enzalutamide improved both rPFS and OS versus placebo in pre-docetaxel mCRPC. The trial included patients with visceral metastases.

name: MAGNITUDE
population: 1L mCRPC with HRD required. Prior ARPI for nmCRPC/mCSPC, or AAP up to 4 months in mCRPC, was allowed. BRCA1/2 subgroup 53%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg QD + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP) vs placebo + AAP
takeaway: Niraparib + AAP improved rPFS but not OS versus AAP in first-line HRR+ mCRPC. The benefit is concentrated in the BRCA subgroup.

name: PROfound
population: mCRPC with progression on enzalutamide or abiraterone; HRR mutation required. Cohort A: ≥1 mutation in BRCA1, BRCA2 or ATM; Cohort B: ≥1 mutation in 12 HRR genes. Visceral mets 27%/35%; prior taxane 65%, prior abiraterone 40%, enzalutamide 40%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs investigator's choice ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Olaparib monotherapy improved rPFS and OS in BRCA/ATM-mutant mCRPC after prior ARPI. Interpret the OS result with caution given 81% crossover.

name: PROpel
population: 1L mCRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutated ~28% (BRCA1 2%/1%, BRCA2 10%/9%); visceral metastases ~12%; prior docetaxel ~22%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP) vs placebo + AAP
endpoints: ⚠️ NR vs NR (28.6% maturity) — HR 0.86 (0.66–1.12), P=0.29 (immature)
takeaway: Adding olaparib to abiraterone improved imaging-based PFS and PFS2 in 1L mCRPC regardless of HRR status, but OS is still immature (28.6% maturity). Benefit concentrates in HRR-mutated disease (HR 0.50 vs 0.76), and adverse events include anemia and VTE.

name: TALAPRO-2
population: 1L metastatic CRPC irrespective of HRR status. HRR-mutated 21%, BRCA1/2 7%, visceral disease 14%, prior taxane 22%.
treatment: Talazoparib 0.5 mg QD + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide
takeaway: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS versus enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC. The benefit was greater in HRR-positive patients (the HRR-negative OS difference was not significant), and haematologic adverse events were significant, more than with olaparib or niraparib.

name: TRITON2
population: Metastatic CRPC with BRCA mutation (n=115) progressing after ARPI and taxane (median 2 prior CRPC treatments). BRCA1 n=13, BRCA2 n=71, germline n=44; prior abiraterone 64.3%, enzalutamide 71.3%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID (single-arm phase 2)
endpoints: 88.7% (IRR-evaluable, stable disease or better); 89.2% (investigator-evaluable, stable disease or better)
takeaway: In this single-arm phase 2 study, rucaparib monotherapy produced an ORR of 43.5% in heavily pretreated BRCA1/2-mutated mCRPC. With no comparator arm, OS is immature and HR is not available.

name: ALSYMPCA
population: mCRPC with symptomatic bone metastases, no visceral metastases (bone only). Received, was ineligible for, or declined docetaxel (57% prior docetaxel); >20 metastases in 30%.
treatment: Radium-223 50 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6 vs placebo
endpoints: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event
takeaway: Radium-223 improved OS and time to first symptomatic skeletal event versus placebo plus best supportive care in symptomatic mCRPC with bone metastases. It was the first OS benefit from a bone-targeted radiopharmaceutical.

name: ERA-223
population: Chemotherapy-naive mCRPC with bone mets and no visceral mets. Prior ARPI excluded.
treatment: Radium-223 + abiraterone acetate/prednisone (AAP) vs placebo + AAP — Ra-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6; AA 1000 mg/d + prednisone 5 mg BID
takeaway: Radium-223 added to abiraterone/prednisone failed to improve symptomatic skeletal-event-free survival, and OS was numerically worse. Fracture risk increased versus AAP alone, so the combination now contradicts use with AAP.

name: PEACE-3
population: First-line mCRPC with bone metastases and no visceral metastases; 30% prior docetaxel.
treatment: Radium-223 + enzalutamide vs enzalutamide alone (open-label): enzalutamide 160 mg/d; Ra-223 55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6; bone-protecting agent mandatory
endpoints: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event
takeaway: Adding radium-223 to enzalutamide improved rPFS and OS compared with enzalutamide alone in first-line mCRPC. A bone-protecting agent was mandatory, and the combination still carried a higher fracture/ONJ risk than enzalutamide alone.

name: CARD
population: mCRPC with prior docetaxel (≥3 cycles) and prior ARSI (abiraterone or enzalutamide) with progression <12 mo. Prior ARPI was abiraterone in 43% and enzalutamide in 56%; Gleason ≥8 in about 60%.
treatment: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² IV q3w vs the alternative ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide)
takeaway: Cabazitaxel improved imaging-based PFS and OS over an alternative ARPI in mCRPC after docetaxel and a first ARPI. It also confirms the poor efficacy of switching to another ARPI after early progression.

name: VISION
population: Metastatic CRPC after ≥1 ARPI and 1–2 taxane regimens; visceral disease ~20%, prior cabazitaxel 38%, 2 prior ARPIs 40%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 + SOC vs SOC alone (SOC excludes chemotherapy, other radioligand therapy, immunotherapy) (2:1)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 plus standard of care improved rPFS and OS over standard of care in post-taxane, post-ARPI, PSMA-PET-selected mCRPC. It led to FDA approval.

name: TheraP
population: Metastatic CRPC after docetaxel; visceral disease 7%, ~90% prior ARPI. Open-label, with crossover of 32% / 20%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs cabazitaxel (open-label)
endpoints: ✅ 5.1 vs 5.1 — HR 0.63 (0.46–0.86), P=0.0028; 1-yr PFS 19% vs 3% (benefit emerges after 6 mo)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 gave better PSA response and PFS than cabazitaxel in post-docetaxel mCRPC (other secondary endpoints were also positive), but with no OS benefit. OS is confounded by crossover (32% / 20%), and reported side effects were thrombocytopenia and dry mouth.

name: PSMAfore
population: Taxane-naive mCRPC progressing on one prior ARPI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, darolutamide or apalutamide); 81% had that ARPI in the CRPC setting. Visceral metastases 13%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 vs switch ARPI (abiraterone/prednisone or enzalutamide); 57% crossover
takeaway: In taxane-naive mCRPC, ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved rPFS and time to symptomatic skeletal event over switching to a second ARPI, but showed no OS difference. OS is confounded by the 57% crossover, so it should not be read as a true absence of survival benefit.

name: TAX 327
population: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing on ADT, chemotherapy-naive, ~90% bone metastases.
treatment: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² Q3W (D3P) vs docetaxel 30 mg/m² weekly (D1P) vs mitoxantrone Q3W (MP), all + prednisone 5 mg BID
takeaway: Three-weekly docetaxel plus prednisone improved OS, pain, PSA response and quality of life versus mitoxantrone in mCRPC. Weekly docetaxel did not improve OS, which is why D3P rather than D1P became the standard of care.

name: BILCAP
population: Resected (R0/R1) biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder cancer), stage I–III (stage II 60%, III 13%/8%). ECOG <2, with ECOG 1 in ~50%.
treatment: Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 q3w for 24 wks vs observation
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine showed an OS benefit in the per-protocol and adjusted sensitivity analyses and is the standard of care. Caveats: the ITT primary OS analysis was not significant (P=0.097), and the RFS benefit appeared only during capecitabine treatment, with recurrences after 24 weeks.

name: FUGA-BT (JCOG1113)
population: Chemotherapy-naive BTC, PS 0–1, enrolled in Japan. ECOG 1 26–31%; metastatic 60%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + S-1 (GS; given indefinitely) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC; cisplatin ×8 cycles, then gemcitabine) — non-inferiority design
takeaway: Gemcitabine + S-1 is non-inferior to gemcitabine + cisplatin in first-line biliary tract cancer. It caused less haematologic toxicity but more mucosal toxicity.

name: KHBO1401-MITSUBA
population: Advanced BTC; adjuvant chemo ≥6 mo allowed; PS 0–2 (no PS 2 in the GCS arm). Enrolled in Japan; metastatic 50%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin + S-1 (GCS) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (GC); both for 24 wks
takeaway: Adding S-1 to gemcitabine + cisplatin improved OS, PFS and ORR in first-line advanced BTC. The trial was conducted in Japan.

name: TOPAZ-1
population: Treatment-naive advanced biliary tract cancer, ECOG PS 0–1, global enrolment. ECOG 0 ~50%, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma ~55%, metastatic ~90%, PD-L1 positive ~60%.
treatment: Durvalumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine/cisplatin; no maintenance gemcitabine
takeaway: Adding durvalumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin improved PFS, OS and ORR in first-line advanced BTC, making it the standard of care.

name: KEYNOTE-966
population: Treatment-naive advanced BTC, ECOG PS 0–1, global enrolment. ECOG 0 43–48%, iCCA 60%, metastatic ~90%, PD-L1 positive ~70%.
treatment: Pembrolizumab + gemcitabine/cisplatin vs placebo + gemcitabine/cisplatin; maintenance gemcitabine-pembrolizumab
takeaway: Adding pembrolizumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin improved OS in first-line advanced BTC. PFS did not meet its significance threshold (P=0.023 vs 0.0125) and ORR was identical between arms, so the result should not be read as positive across the board.

name: ABC-02
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer, PS 0–2, UK. ECOG 2 in ~10%; metastatic disease in ~75%.
treatment: Gemcitabine + cisplatin (GemCis, GC) vs gemcitabine alone — up to 8 cycles (24 wks)
takeaway: Gemcitabine plus cisplatin beat gemcitabine alone on both OS and PFS, making GemCis the standard of care in first-line advanced BTC.

name: ABC-06
population: Advanced biliary tract cancer with progressive disease on first-line GemCis. ECOG 0–1, UK.
treatment: FOLFOX + active symptom control (ASC) vs ASC alone — FOLFOX up to 12 cycles
endpoints: 4.0 mo (FOLFOX arm only; no routine imaging in ASC-alone arm)
takeaway: FOLFOX plus ASC improved OS over ASC alone in second-line advanced BTC, making it the second-line standard of care. Caveat: the benefit is driven by the 6- and 12-month OS tail.

name: ClarIDHy
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment and an IDH1 mutation.
treatment: Ivosidenib vs placebo (2:1); 57% crossover
takeaway: Ivosidenib improved PFS versus placebo in IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma treated in the second line or later. ITT OS was not significant because of 57% crossover, but the RPSFT crossover-adjusted analysis showed an OS benefit.

name: HERIZON-GEA-01
population: Previously untreated, HER2-positive (IHC3+ or IHC2+/ISH+) unresectable locally advanced/recurrent/metastatic gastric, GEJ, or esophageal adenocarcinoma.
treatment: Zanidatamab + tislelizumab + chemo vs zanidatamab + chemo vs trastuzumab + chemo (comparator), 1:1:1
endpoints: ⚠️ Zani-ChT 24.4 vs trastuzumab-ChT 19.2 — HR 0.80 (0.64–1.01), P=0.06 (NS at this interim)
takeaway: Both zanidatamab-containing regimens (with or without tislelizumab) improved PFS over the 15-year-old trastuzumab + chemo standard in first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. At the first OS interim the triplet with tislelizumab also improved OS, but the zanidatamab + chemo doublet's OS was not yet significant (further analyses planned). Diarrhea is the dominant adverse event with zanidatamab-based regimens.

name: KEYNOTE-158
cancer: Endometrial CA / GC / BTC / Pancreas / Other
population: MSI-H/dMMR non-colorectal solid tumors (cholangiocarcinoma n=22, 9.4%) with progression on ≥1 prior therapy.
treatment: Pembrolizumab monotherapy (single-arm)
takeaway: Pembrolizumab produced an ORR of 34.3% in previously treated MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors, including 40.9% in cholangiocarcinoma, with OS better than a historical chemotherapy control. It carries a tumor-agnostic FDA approval for dMMR/MSI-H cancers.

name: NIFTY
population: Metastatic biliary tract cancer with progression on 1L gemcitabine–cisplatin. ECOG 0–1; South Korea.
treatment: Liposomal irinotecan + 5-FU/LV vs 5-FU/LV alone — chemotherapy continued indefinitely
takeaway: Liposomal irinotecan + 5-FU/LV improved both PFS and OS over 5-FU/LV alone in second-line metastatic biliary tract cancer. The response-rate difference was only a trend (P=0.068).

name: VISION
population: Metastatic NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping mutation (liquid and/or tissue biopsy); ≤2 prior lines, ECOG 0–1; stable/treated brain metastases 11%.
treatment: Tepotinib monotherapy (single-arm)
takeaway: Tepotinib produced an ORR of 46% in MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC in this single-arm phase 2 trial, with similar responses by liquid and tissue biopsy. Peripheral edema was a class adverse effect.

name: LUMINOSITY
population: Advanced/metastatic c-Met protein-overexpressing (IHC ≥25% 3+), nonsquamous EGFR-wildtype NSCLC; ≤2 prior lines (≤1 prior cytotoxic chemo), ECOG 0–1. Heavily pretreated: 98% prior platinum, 82% prior ICI.
treatment: Telisotuzumab vedotin (Teliso-V) monotherapy (single-arm)
endpoints: 5.7 mo (4.6–6.9) c-Met OE total; 5.5 (4.1–8.3) c-Met high; 6.0 (4.5–8.1) c-Met intermediate
14.5 mo (9.9–16.6) c-Met OE total; 14.6 c-Met high; 14.2 c-Met intermediate
takeaway: Telisotuzumab vedotin (c-Met-directed ADC, MMAE payload) monotherapy achieved an ORR of 28.6% (34.6% in c-Met high) in previously treated, c-Met protein-overexpressing, nonsquamous EGFR-wildtype NSCLC. Selection by protein expression (IHC), distinct from MET exon 14/amplification-driven approaches, gives a larger (~25%) eligible population. The squamous and EGFR-mutant cohorts closed for futility; the results support an ongoing phase 3 vs docetaxel.

name: FIGHT-202
population: Cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment and FGFR2 fusion; other FGFR2 alterations enrolled as a comparator cohort.
treatment: Pemigatinib monotherapy (single-arm; pan-FGFR1-3 TKI)
endpoints: ✅ FGFR2 fusion 35.5% vs 0% in both other cohorts
takeaway: Pemigatinib achieved an ORR of 35.5% in second-line-or-later FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma, with PFS and OS that look favourable against a historical chemotherapy control. ORR was 0% in the other FGF/FGFR alterations, and hyperphosphatemia is the class toxicity.

name: FOENIX-CCA2
population: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with ≥1 prior treatment and FGFR2 fusion; 57% had ≥2 prior treatments.
treatment: Futibatinib monotherapy (single-arm; irreversible pan-FGFR1-4 TKI)
takeaway: Futibatinib achieved an ORR of 42% in second-line-or-later FGFR2-fusion intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in a single-arm trial.

name: ROAR
population: Previously treated advanced rare cancers with BRAF V600E mutation; no prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor (N=206).
treatment: Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg QD (single-arm basket, no control)
endpoints: ✅ ATC 56%, BTC 53%, LGG 54%, HGG 33%, ASI 67% (2/3), HCL 89%, MM 50%, GIST 0% (1 pt, SD)
ATC 6.7, BTC 9.0, HGG 5.5, ASI 9.5, MM 6.3 mo; LGG, HCL NE
ATC 14.5, BTC 13.5, HGG 17.6, ASI 21.8, MM 33.9 mo; LGG, HCL NE
ATC 14.4, BTC 8.9, HGG 31.2, MM 11.1, ASI 7.7 mo; LGG/HCL NR
takeaway: Dabrafenib plus trametinib produced an ORR of about 50% in previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant rare cancers in this single-arm basket trial. The row notes an FDA tumor-agnostic approval for BRAF V600E-mutant cancers, with CRC expected to be an exception.

name: PSMAddition
population: PSMA-PET-positive mHSPC (no PSMA-negative lesion exclusion); treatment-naive or ≤45 days of ARPI/ADT (90%). High-volume 68%, de novo 50%, visceral (lung/liver) 15%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 (7.4 GBq ±10% ×6) + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI (1:1, open-label; crossover 16%)
endpoints: ✅ NR vs NR (interim; 24% vs 30% events) — HR 0.72 (0.58–0.90), P=0.0021
⏳ NR vs NR (interim, immature) — HR 0.84 (0.63–1.13), P=0.13
takeaway: This is the first phase 3 radioligand therapy trial in mHSPC, and adding ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 to ADT + ARPI improved rPFS in first-line disease. OS is immature, and the combination caused more adverse events (dry mouth, cytopenias, GI) with a HRQoL time-to-worsening HR of about 1.1.

name: AMPLITUDE
population: mCSPC with HRD required. BRCA1/2 in 56%, high-volume disease 78%, prior docetaxel 16%.
treatment: Niraparib 200 mg + abiraterone 1000 mg (dual-action tablet) + prednisone 5 mg QD vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone (AAP)
takeaway: Niraparib plus AAP improved rPFS over AAP in HRR-positive mCSPC, but OS is still immature. The benefit is concentrated in BRCA-altered disease (non-BRCA HR 0.81, post hoc), and anemia and hypertension are the toxicities to watch.

name: ARIEL3
population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer (HGSC/EC) with CA-125 <ULN, enrolled regardless of HRD/BRCA status. BRCAm 35%, HRD 63%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
endpoints: BRCAm 38% vs 9%; HRD 27% vs 7%; ITT 18% vs 8%
takeaway: Rucaparib improved PFS in platinum-sensitive second-line disease regardless of BRCA/HRD status. There was no OS benefit.

name: ARROW
population: Advanced/metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC, treatment-naive or post-platinum. Efficacy population N=281; history of brain metastases 35%; KIF5B fusion 70%.
treatment: Pralsetinib 400 mg QD (single-arm)
takeaway: Pralsetinib gave an ORR of 70%, median DoR 19.1 mo and median OS 44.3 mo at final analysis, leading to FDA approval in 2020 (accelerated) and 2023 (regular). Cytopenia, pneumonitis and infection are the toxicities to watch, and KIF5B-RET carries a poorer prognosis.

name: ATHENA-MONO
population: FIGO III–IV HGSC/EC, fallopian/peritoneal cancer, enrolled regardless of HRD status. CR ~55%, stage III 76%, HRD 43%.
treatment: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs placebo (4:1), up to 2 years
endpoints: ITT 48.8% vs 9.1%; HRD 58.8% vs 20.0% (not formally tested)
takeaway: Rucaparib maintenance after first-line chemotherapy improved PFS in the HRD, ITT (HR 0.52) and HRD-negative (HR 0.65) populations. It covers the broadest first-line PARPi population, allowing R0 resection and with 79% BRCA wild-type.

name: AcceleRET-Lung
population: Treatment-naive RET fusion-positive metastatic NSCLC, ECOG 0–1. Europe 71%; history of CNS metastases 28%. Terminated by sponsor at 98.7% accrual.
treatment: Pralsetinib (n=110) vs platinum-based chemo ± pembrolizumab (n=113)
endpoints: ❌ NR vs 39.8 mo — HR 1.09 (0.65–1.85); P=0.742 (immature; 34% crossover)
takeaway: First-line pralsetinib beat platinum-based chemotherapy on PFS (18.7 vs 9.0 mo), ORR and DoR in RET fusion-positive NSCLC, though OS is immature with 34% crossover. There was an infection signal (fatal 7.4%), which led to a protocol amendment in October 2024 to strengthen monitoring.

name: AtTEnd
population: Newly diagnosed residual/inoperable stage III–IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (no prior chemo for recurrence; prior adjuvant platinum OK if PFI ≥6 mo); carcinosarcoma allowed; ECOG 0–2. Recurrent 67%, Asian 20%, central dMMR 23%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg + carboplatin/paclitaxel q3w ×6–8 → atezolizumab q3w until PD vs placebo + carboplatin/paclitaxel → placebo (2:1)
endpoints: ⚠️ 38.7 vs 30.2 mo — HR 0.82 (0.63–1.07); P=0.048 (boundary 0.024); interim, not significant
↔ No difference by MMR or PD-L1 status (data in appendix)
takeaway: Atezolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by atezolizumab improved PFS in first-line endometrial cancer, driven by dMMR (HR 0.36; overall HR 0.74). There was no benefit in pMMR (PFS HR 0.92, OS HR 1.00), unlike RUBY, GY018 and DUO-E, and OS is an interim analysis that is not significant.

name: CABINET
population: G1–3 neuroendocrine tumours with progression on ≥1 prior therapy (besides SSA) within 1 yr; epNET n=203 (GI 57%, lung 19%) and pNET n=95. About 60% had prior Lu-177.
treatment: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1) in two cohorts, extrapancreatic NET (epNET) and pancreatic NET (pNET); crossover allowed
takeaway: Cabozantinib improved PFS and ORR over placebo in both pancreatic and extrapancreatic NET after prior Lu-177/everolimus. OS is immature because the trial stopped after the first interim analysis and crossover was 33–41%, and dose reduction was needed in 60% of patients.

name: CARES-005
population: Unresectable HCC treatable with TACE (CNLC Ib–IIIa, i.e. BCLC A–C without extrahepatic mets), Child-Pugh A; China only. BCLC C 43%, PVTT Vp3–4 27%, beyond up-to-7 90%, HBV 80%.
treatment: TACE + camrelizumab 200 mg q3w + rivoceranib (apatinib) 250 mg QD vs TACE alone (on-demand cTACE; crossover allowed at progression)
endpoints: ✅ 10.8 vs 3.2 — HR 0.34 (0.24–0.50), P<0.001 (composite of RECICL + CP-C + TACE failure/refractoriness)
⏳ 24.0 vs 21.5 — HR 0.87 (0.57–1.32), P=0.50; immature (90 deaths), 75% of TACE-arm progressors crossed over
