takeaway: TACE plus camrelizumab and rivoceranib gave PFS of 10.8 vs 3.2 months (HR 0.34) over TACE alone, and it is the only TACE-combination trial enrolling BCLC C / Vp3–4 PVTT (27%). OS is immature and confounded by 75% crossover; this is a phase II, open-label, investigator-assessed, China-only study.

name: CLARINET
population: Non-functioning, SSTR+ GEP-NET, G1–2 (Ki-67 <10%), G1 ~70%; pancreas 45%, midgut 36%. 96% had SD at baseline and 84% were treatment-naive.
treatment: Lanreotide 120 mg SC q28d vs placebo, up to 96 wk (24 doses)
takeaway: Lanreotide improved PFS over placebo in SSTR+ non-functioning G1–2 GEP-NET. Benefit despite mostly stable disease at baseline supports starting SSA early; OS was not significant, with 46% crossover.

name: CREATE-X
population: HER2-negative stage I–IIIB breast cancer with non-pCR after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Japan + South Korea). HR+ 68%, TNBC 32%; stage IIIA–IIIB ~40%.
treatment: Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID D1–14 Q3W ×6–8 cycles + standard therapy vs standard therapy alone
takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine for 6–8 cycles in HER2-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy improved both DFS and OS. The benefit was concentrated in TNBC; in HR+ disease the DFS and OS differences were not significant.

name: DUO-E
population: Newly diagnosed measurable stage III / stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (1L; prior adjuvant chemotherapy allowed if relapse ≥12 mo); carcinosarcoma allowed. pMMR 80%, recurrent 52%, PD-L1+ (TAP ≥1%) ~67%.
treatment: Carboplatin/paclitaxel + durvalumab → durvalumab + olaparib vs CP + durvalumab → durvalumab vs CP + placebo (3 arms, 1:1:1)
endpoints: ✅ D+O 15.1 vs D 10.2 vs control 9.6 — D+O vs control HR 0.55 (0.43–0.69), P<0.0001; D vs control HR 0.71 (0.57–0.89), P=0.003
⚠️ NR vs NR vs 25.9 (IA1, 28% maturity) — D+O HR 0.59 (0.42–0.83), P=0.003; D HR 0.77 (0.56–1.07), P=0.12 (interim, not significant)
takeaway: Adding durvalumab to carboplatin/paclitaxel, with or without olaparib, improved PFS in first-line endometrial cancer. Olaparib adds benefit mainly in pMMR (HR 0.76 vs durvalumab) and PD-L1+ disease, and none in dMMR (HR 0.97). The PD-L1-negative subgroup had little benefit and OS is immature.

name: ECOG-ACRIN E2211
population: Advanced/unresectable pancreatic NET, low/intermediate grade, radiographic progression within 12 mo. No prior temozolomide, DTIC, capecitabine or 5-FU; prior SSA 63%, everolimus ~35%, sunitinib ~10%; liver mets 94%.
treatment: CAPTEM (capecitabine 750 mg/m² BID D1–14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² D10–14, q28d) vs temozolomide alone (200 mg/m² D1–5, q28d), up to 13 cycles
takeaway: This is the only randomized trial of CAPTEM in pancreatic NET: adding capecitabine lengthened PFS (22.7 vs 14.4 mo, HR 0.58) with the highest ORR (~40%) of any randomized pNET regimen. The OS gain (~5 mo) was not significant and toxicity doubled (Grade 3–4 45% vs 22%). MGMT deficiency predicts response (IHC-low ORR 52% vs 15%), so test it when tumour shrinkage is the goal.

name: EMERALD-1
population: Unresectable HCC amenable to TACE, no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A–B7; Vp3/Vp4 excluded. BCLC A 26% / B 57% / C 16%; beyond up-to-7 52%; PVI (Vp1–2) 7%.
treatment: TACE + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w → durvalumab 1120 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w (bev only ≥14 d after last TACE) vs TACE + durvalumab + placebo vs TACE + placebo
endpoints: ⏳ Not reported (interim OS not significant; still masked)
takeaway: This was the first positive phase 3 of systemic therapy plus TACE: durvalumab + bevacizumab + TACE reached PFS 15.0 vs 8.2 mo (HR 0.77). Durvalumab alone with TACE did not help, so the anti-VEGF partner matters. OS has not yet been reported.

name: EMERALD-3
population: Embolisation-eligible unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A, no Vp3/Vp4; ≤1 prior palliative embolisation. BCLC A 20% / B 62% / C 18%; beyond up-to-7 62%; Asian 72%.
treatment: STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg ×1 + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w) + lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + TACE vs STRIDE + TACE vs TACE alone (open-label, sponsor-blinded)
endpoints: 12.9 vs 8.1 (first 175; descriptive) — HR 0.71 (0.56–0.91), not formally tested
NR vs 32.9 (descriptive) — HR 0.70 (0.51–0.95), not formally tested
takeaway: STRIDE + lenvatinib + TACE improved PFS over TACE alone (13.0 vs 9.8 mo, HR 0.70), but the OS HR of 0.84 was not significant at interim. STRIDE + TACE without lenvatinib looked as good (PFS HR 0.71, OS HR 0.70) with less toxicity, although it was not formally tested. Lenvatinib added grade 3–4 TRAEs, discontinuations and deaths.

name: GOG-229E
population: Recurrent/persistent endometrial cancer after 1–2 prior cytotoxic regimens; measurable disease; GOG PS 0–2; no prior VEGF-targeted therapy. Serous 27%, grade 3 71%, 2 prior regimens 37%.
treatment: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w (single-arm, no control)
takeaway: Single-agent bevacizumab in second- or third-line endometrial cancer met its 6-month PFS criterion (40%, best among GOG historical controls), though ORR was only 13.5%. Responses occurred across histologies (4/7 in serous). High plasma VEGF-A was associated with no response and worse OS (exploratory).

name: GOG0209
population: Chemo-naive stage III/IV or recurrent endometrial cancer with poor potential for cure by surgery/RT; GOG PS 0–2. Measurable or recurrent disease in 61%; non-measurable stage III/IV allowed from 2006.
treatment: Paclitaxel 175 + carboplatin AUC 6 (TC) q3w ×7 vs TAP (doxorubicin 45 + cisplatin 50 d1, paclitaxel 160 d2 + G-CSF) q3w ×7
takeaway: Carboplatin + paclitaxel was non-inferior to TAP for OS and PFS, with less toxicity and slightly better QoL. TC is the first-line standard for advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer and the backbone for later ICI trials (GY018, RUBY, DUO-E).

name: IMvigor010
population: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (bladder 93%, UTUC 7%) after radical surgery + LND: ypT2–4a/ypN+ post-NAC, or pT3–4a/pN+ without NAC (cisplatin-ineligible/declined). pN+ 52%; prior NAC 48%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W ×1 yr vs observation
takeaway: The first phase 3 adjuvant ICI trial in muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma was negative for DFS and OS, with no benefit by PD-L1. In the exploratory analysis, ctDNA-positive patients (37%) had an OS benefit with atezolizumab (HR 0.59) while ctDNA-negative patients had no benefit and more adverse events; this was prospectively tested in IMvigor011.

name: IMvigor011
population: MIBC post-cystectomy, (y)pT2–4aN0 or (y)pT0–4aN+, no radiologic disease; ECOG 0–2. 761 enrolled in ctDNA surveillance (q6w ×9 mo + 1 yr), of whom 250 ctDNA+ were randomized; N+ 57%, T3/T4 72%.
treatment: Atezolizumab 1680 mg Q4W ×1 yr vs placebo (2:1), only if ctDNA+ on serial monitoring
takeaway: This is the first prospective ctDNA-guided adjuvant RCT, showing both DFS and OS benefit with atezolizumab in ctDNA-positive patients, with OS benefit regardless of PD-L1. Persistent ctDNA-negative patients had 2-yr DFS of 88% without treatment, supporting de-escalation; follow-up is short (16.1 mo).

name: IMvigor130
population: Both cisplatin-eligible and -ineligible patients. Carboplatin 70% (arm A) / 66% (arm C); UTUC 27%. Arm B restricted to IC2/3 after Apr 2018.
treatment: Atezolizumab + platinum-gemcitabine (A) vs atezolizumab monotherapy (B) vs placebo + platinum-gemcitabine (C)
endpoints: OS, B vs C in IC2/3
A vs C 65% vs 60%; B vs C 38% vs 59%
takeaway: Atezolizumab added to platinum-gemcitabine improved PFS, but the final OS was negative (A vs C HR 0.85). Atezolizumab monotherapy had OS similar to chemotherapy in the ITT population, with a signal only in PD-L1 IC2/3 cisplatin-ineligible patients (HR 0.56, post-hoc). In the cisplatin subgroup OS was 21.5 vs 13.4 (HR 0.76, exploratory), which supports a cisplatin-based ICI combination.

name: KEYNOTE-775
population: Advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer after 1 prior platinum (2 allowed if one was (neo)adjuvant); no prior ICI or VEGF-targeted therapy; any histology except carcinosarcoma/sarcoma; ECOG 0–1. pMMR 84%, serous 26%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 20 mg QD + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (≤35 doses) vs treatment of physician's choice: doxorubicin 60 q3w or weekly paclitaxel 80 (3 on / 1 off)
takeaway: After platinum in endometrial cancer, lenvatinib + pembrolizumab improved PFS, OS and ORR over doxorubicin/paclitaxel, including in pMMR disease (OS HR 0.68). It is toxic: grade ≥3 adverse events 89%, lenvatinib dose reduction in two-thirds, and hypothyroidism 57%.

name: KEYNOTE-868 (NRG-GY018)
population: Measurable stage III/IVA, or stage IVB / recurrent endometrial cancer (± measurable); prior adjuvant chemo allowed if ≥12 mo; carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG 0–2. Separate dMMR (n=225) and pMMR (n=591) cohorts.
treatment: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + CP ×6 → pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤14 cycles) vs placebo + CP → placebo
takeaway: Pembrolizumab + CP followed by pembrolizumab maintenance improved PFS in first-line advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer in both cohorts (dMMR HR 0.30, pMMR HR 0.54), with no excess chemotherapy toxicity and immune-related AEs as expected. OS is immature, and pMMR median follow-up is only 7.9 mo.

name: KEYNOTE-B15 / EV-304
population: Cisplatin-eligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer (cT2–T4aN0 or T1–T4aN1), ECOG 0–1. T3N0/T4aN0 ~72%; CPS ≥10 ~57%.
treatment: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (neoadjuvant ×4 → surgery → adjuvant EV ×5 + pembrolizumab ×13) vs cisplatin-gemcitabine (neoadjuvant ×4) → surgery
takeaway: EFS, OS and pCR were all positive versus cisplatin-gemcitabine neoadjuvant chemotherapy, making this the first non-platinum regimen to beat cisplatin-based NAC. Together with KN-905, it supports perioperative EV-pembrolizumab regardless of cisplatin eligibility. Caveats: the control arm has no perioperative ICI (cf. NIAGARA), and the experimental arm has more AEs and longer treatment.

name: LAURA
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (AJCC 8th) with EGFR Ex19del or L858R, no progression after platinum-based chemo and RT. Asian 82%; L858R 41–48%.
treatment: Osimertinib 80 mg QD vs placebo (2:1) until progression; crossover allowed
takeaway: Osimertinib after chemoradiation markedly improved PFS in EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III NSCLC, so EGFR should be tested before chemoRT. OS is immature (20% maturity) and confounded by 81% crossover.

name: LEAP-012
population: Unresectable, non-metastatic HCC amenable to TACE, Child-Pugh A, no portal vein invasion or extrahepatic disease. Excluded tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours or ≥50% of liver. BCLC A 31% / B 59% / C 10%; tumour burden score ≤6 48%.
treatment: Lenvatinib 8/12 mg QD + pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (≤2 yr) + TACE vs dual placebo + TACE; systemic therapy started 2–4 wk before first TACE
endpoints: ⚠️ Interim: median not reported, 24-mo 75% vs 69% — HR 0.80 (0.57–1.11), P=0.087 (boundary 0.0012)
takeaway: Adding lenvatinib + pembrolizumab to TACE improved PFS (14.6 vs 10.0 mo, HR 0.66), but OS, a dual primary endpoint, was not significant at interim and the trial later announced closure for low likelihood of meeting the OS threshold. Toxicity was heavy, with grade ≥3 TRAEs in 71%.

name: LIBRETTO-001
population: RET fusion-positive NSCLC and thyroid cancer, RET-mutant MTC, and other RET fusion-positive solid tumors (tumor-agnostic). N=796 across all cohorts.
treatment: Selpercatinib 160 mg BID (single-arm, multi-cohort basket)
endpoints: NSCLC naive 22.0 mo, post-platinum 24.9 mo; tumor-agnostic 13.2 mo
takeaway: Selpercatinib produced high response rates across RET fusion-positive NSCLC and thyroid cancer and RET-mutant MTC, leading to FDA approval in 2020 and a tumor-agnostic approval in September 2022. Colorectal cancer responded less well (ORR 20%, DoR 9.4 mo).

name: LIBRETTO-431
population: Treatment-naive advanced/metastatic non-squamous RET fusion-positive NSCLC; optional crossover at progression. Brain mets 22%.
treatment: Selpercatinib (n=159) vs platinum + pemetrexed ± pembrolizumab (n=102)
endpoints: 84% vs 65%; mDoR 24.2 vs 11.5 mo; CNS ORR 82% vs 58%
takeaway: First-line selpercatinib beat chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab on PFS (24.8 vs 11.2 mo), establishing the first-line standard of care, and markedly reduced CNS progression. Monitor LFTs and blood pressure.

name: LIBRETTO-432
population: Stage IB–IIIA RET fusion-positive NSCLC after definitive therapy (surgery or RT ± adjuvant chemo). Primary analysis in stage II–IIIA (n=109). East Asia ≈57%; prior systemic therapy ≈91%.
treatment: Selpercatinib up to 3 yr (n=75) vs placebo (n=76)
takeaway: First adjuvant targeted therapy for RET fusion-positive NSCLC, with a large EFS benefit (HR 0.17). OS is immature, EFS is not a cure, and LFT elevation is common.

name: LIBRETTO-531
population: Kinase inhibitor-naive advanced/metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC); optional crossover at progression.
treatment: Selpercatinib (n=193) vs cabozantinib or vandetanib (n=98)
takeaway: Selpercatinib beat cabozantinib or vandetanib on PFS (HR 0.28) and ORR in first-line RET-mutant MTC, leading to FDA regular approval, and was better tolerated.

name: MITO END-2
population: Advanced (FIGO III–IV) or recurrent endometrial cancer, measurable or evaluable; ≤1 prior platinum line (≥6 mo interval); carcinosarcoma excluded; ECOG ≤2. Recurrent ~62%, G3 ~50%, serous/clear cell 16%, prior ChT 24%.
treatment: Carboplatin–paclitaxel + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bev maintenance vs carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 q3w × 6–8
endpoints: ❌ 13.7 vs 10.5 — HR 0.84 (0.5–1.3), P=0.43 (log-rank NS); ⚠️ post-hoc Breslow test P=0.08 (study α 0.20)
takeaway: Adding bevacizumab to carboplatin–paclitaxel in advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer did not meet the primary PFS endpoint, though ORR, 6-month DCR and OS were numerically higher. Thromboembolism, hypertension and discontinuations were more frequent, and this was a small phase II without molecular stratification.

name: NCT01367002 (HER2+ USC)
population: HER2+ (IHC 3+ or 2+/FISH+) uterine serous carcinoma, stage III–IV after surgery (71%) or measurable recurrent (29%; PFI >6 mo, ≤3 prior ChT); ECOG 0–2. Central HER2 review; control arm older (median 73 vs 66).
treatment: Carboplatin–paclitaxel + trastuzumab (8 → 6 mg/kg q3w) × 6 → trastuzumab maintenance until PD vs carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 q3w × 6
takeaway: Adding trastuzumab to carboplatin–paclitaxel in HER2+ uterine serous carcinoma improved PFS (HR 0.46) and OS (HR 0.58) with no added toxicity. The benefit was largest in stage III–IV primary disease, with no OS gain in recurrent disease; this was a small phase II (n=58) with one-sided α 0.10 that closed early for slow accrual.

name: NETTER-1
population: G1–2 SSTR+ midgut NET with progression on standard octreotide LAR. Ileum 74%; liver mets 83%; G1 69%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w ×4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in somatostatin-analogue-refractory midgut NET, making it standard of care. The OS difference was not significant, with 36% crossover; adverse events include cytopenia and MDS.

name: NETTER-2
population: Treatment-naive G2–3 SSTR+ GEP-NET. Pancreas 54%, small intestine 29%; G3 35%; liver mets 90%.
treatment: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV q8w ×4 + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg q4w (2:1)
takeaway: ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate improved PFS and ORR in first-line higher-grade GEP-NET. The 43% ORR (CR 5%) is unusual for NET, and OS is immature.

name: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16)
population: Predominantly HGSC in two cohorts: gBRCA (n=203) and non-gBRCA (n=350), the latter tested for HRD (myChoice).
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Niraparib improved PFS in both the gBRCA cohort (HR 0.27) and the non-gBRCA cohort (HR 0.45) in 2L/3L ovarian cancer. There was no OS benefit, and grade ≥3 thrombocytopenia occurred in 34%.

name: PACIFIC
population: Unresectable stage III NSCLC (IASLC 7th) with no progression after ≥2 cycles of platinum-based CCRT. Unselected for PD-L1 (TC ≥25% 22%, <25% 41%, unknown 37%); EGFR mutant 6%.
treatment: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg Q2W for up to 12 mo vs placebo (2:1), consolidation starting 1–42 days after chemoRT
takeaway: One year of consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiation improved PFS and OS in unresectable stage III NSCLC and is standard of care. Benefit was seen regardless of PD-L1, though it was smaller in EGFR-mutant disease, and it should be started within 14 days after CRT.

name: PRIMA
population: High-risk FIGO III–IV HGSC/endometrioid, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer, regardless of HRD status; prior bevacizumab allowed. CR 70%, stage III 65%, HRD 51%; NACT 67%.
treatment: Niraparib 300 mg QD vs placebo (2:1), up to 3 years; niraparib dose adjusted by body weight and platelets
takeaway: Niraparib maintenance after first-line chemotherapy in high-risk ovarian cancer improved PFS regardless of HRD status, but OS was not improved. Grade ≥3 haematological adverse events were frequent.

name: PROMID
population: Treatment-naive G1–2 midgut NET. Ki-67 ≤2% in 95%; functional 39%; SSA scan positive 75%; hepatic tumour burden ≤10% in ~75%.
treatment: Octreotide LAR 30 mg IM q28d vs placebo, until PFS event
takeaway: Octreotide LAR lengthened time to progression in first-line functional and non-functional midgut NET and is standard of care. As the very first SSA trial, it showed the drug works in both settings, so it is anti-proliferative and not just for symptom control.

name: RADIANT-2
population: Grade 1–2 functional GI-NET with progression within 1 year. Small intestine 52%, lung 10%, colon 7%; prior SSA 79%, prior chemotherapy 30%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily + octreotide LAR 30 mg vs placebo + octreotide LAR 30 mg q28d
takeaway: Everolimus added to octreotide in functional GI-NET missed the prespecified PFS significance boundary, so the trial is negative. The row points to RADIANT-4, which tested everolimus in non-functional NETs.

name: RADIANT-3
population: Grade 1–2 pancreatic NET with progression within 1 year. Well differentiated 83%, liver metastases 92%, functional 24%; prior chemotherapy 50%, prior SSA 49%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo, both with best supportive care (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in progressive pNET and became the standard of care as second-line therapy. Most disease was stabilised rather than shrunk (ORR 5%), and toxicities include stomatitis, hyperglycemia and ILD.

name: RADIANT-4
population: Grade 1–2 non-functional GI or lung NET. Lung 30%, GI 58%, unknown primary 12%; prior SSA >50%, prior chemotherapy ~25%.
treatment: Everolimus 10 mg PO daily vs placebo (2:1), both with best supportive care
takeaway: Everolimus improved PFS in non-functional GI and lung NETs and is the standard of care as second-line therapy. OS showed only a trend that was not significant at the first interim analysis (HR 0.64, boundary P 0.0002).

name: RUBY
population: Primary advanced stage III–IV (not amenable to cure) or first-recurrence endometrial cancer; carcinosarcoma allowed. dMMR/MSI-H 24%; recurrent 48%, primary stage IV 34%, stage III 19%.
treatment: Dostarlimab 500 mg + carboplatin-paclitaxel (CP) q3w ×6 → dostarlimab 1000 mg q6w (≤3 yr) vs placebo + CP → placebo
takeaway: Adding dostarlimab to carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS in first-line advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, with the largest benefit in dMMR (HR 0.28) and a smaller one in pMMR (HR 0.76). The OS signal is favorable (HR 0.64) but comes from an interim analysis and did not cross its boundary.

name: SOLO-1
population: FIGO III–IV high-grade serous/endometrioid, fallopian or peritoneal cancer with BRCA1/2 mutation; prior bevacizumab excluded. Baseline: CR 82%, stage III 83%, BRCA1 72%.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1), up to 2 years (longer if PR)
takeaway: Olaparib maintenance in first-line after TC chemotherapy in BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer improved PFS, with the PFS benefit sustained after the 2-year stop. The OS benefit did not cross the significance boundary (p=.0004 vs 0.0001 required).

name: SOLO-2
population: High-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer with germline BRCA mutation.
treatment: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs placebo (2:1)
takeaway: Olaparib improved PFS in germline BRCA-mutated disease. OS was not significant in the unadjusted analysis but was significant when adjusted for the 38% crossover, and long exposure carried an 8% MDS/AML rate.

name: SUN1111
population: Grade 1–2 pancreatic NET with progression within 1 year; prior chemotherapy 69%, prior SSA 36%, functional tumours ~50%. No prior TKI/VEGF inhibitor.
treatment: Sunitinib 37.5 mg PO daily (continuous) vs placebo, both with BSC (SSA allowed)
takeaway: Sunitinib improved PFS and ORR in progressive pancreatic NET, with an immature OS signal. The trial stopped early because of toxicity in the placebo arm, and the benefit was shown only in pancreatic NET, not in GI-NET.
